title: The Real Reason You Automatically Follow People's Gaze
hook: Your brain is hardwired to track where others look.

narration.text: Your brain is hardwired to track where others look.
This unconscious social cue, called 'gaze following', is a fundamental human instinct.
It helps us quickly assess potential threats or points of interest in our environment.
From birth, we're primed to interpret others' visual attention for survival.
You might notice yourself doing this in crowded places or unfamiliar settings.
It is a silent, ancient form of communication, guiding our focus.
Try to notice it next time you are out, and tell us in the comments if it worked on you, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Ever wondered why you automatically look where other people are looking? This short explains the fascinating, unconscious social cue of gaze following, a hardwired instinct that shapes how we interact with the world and each other. Discover the evolutionary reasons behind this everyday phenomenon.
topic: Why people automatically tend to follow where others are looking, an unconscious social cue.
